test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-II Official Paper-I (Held On: 20 Jan, 2025)
subject: general
question:
Complete the dialogue for Person B using the correct idiom.

Person A: We are all going to the club this weekend. Do you want to come?

Person B: Thank you for asking. But I don’t like clubs. It’s ______.

options.text: not my cup, not my tea

solution:
The correct answer is '**not my cup of tea**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom "**not my cup of tea**" means something that one does not like or is not interested in.
 
• In this dialogue, Person B is expressing that they do not enjoy going to clubs, so this idiom is appropriate.
 
• **Options 1, 2**, and 4 are incorrect as they either modify the idiom in a non-standard way or use incorrect versions.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Complete Dialogue:** *"Person A: We are all going to the club this weekend. Do you want to come? Person B: Thank you for asking. But I don’t like clubs. It’s **not my cup of tea**__."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "my cup of coffee"** is incorrect because the standard idiom is "cup of tea", not "cup of coffee".
 
• **Option 2: "not my cup of coffee"** is incorrect; again, the idiom traditionally uses "cup of tea".
 
• **Option 4: "not my cup, not my tea"** is incorrect because it is not a recognized idiom.
